section_summary: This section consists of U.S. Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI) reports, attaché summaries, and State Department Division of Far Eastern Affairs analytical memoranda dating primarily from March 1932 to March 1933 (with an isolated 1928 naval aviation report). The documents trace the escalating dominance of the Japanese military over civil cabinets, the consolidation of Manchuria and Manchukuo, border frictions around Shanhaikwan and the Soviet frontier, and growing ideological extremism and domestic fascism. They also examine diplomatic confrontations at the League of Nations over the Lytton Report, Japanese-American strategic tensions in the Pacific and Hawaii, constitutional clashes over the Emperor's Supreme Command prerogative, and Japan's worsening financial strain and industrial reorganization.

subfiles.about: An attaché report recording the experimental sinking of the decommissioned destroyer Hatsuharu by naval aircraft in Tokyo Bay.
subfiles.from: Naval Attaché, Tokyo / Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.summary: ONI report: the decommissioned destroyer Hatsuharu was sunk by carrier-based bombing off Tokyo Bay in August 1928, observed by the assembled Combined Fleet and Navy Minister.
subfiles.title: ONI Attaché Report: Old Destroyer Hatsuharu Sunk by Airplane Bombs
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence, Navy Department

subfiles.about: A confidential ONI memorandum relaying a Tokyo dispatch that forecasts a new national cabinet under Privy Councillor Baron Hiranuma.
subfiles.from: Office of Naval Intelligence, Navy Department
subfiles.summary: ONI memo relays Naval Attaché's prediction that a national-unity cabinet under Baron Hiranuma would follow the Diet's adjournment, with a War Minister change expected not to cost military prestige.
subfiles.title: ONI Memorandum: Confidential Dispatch on Prospective Cabinet Headed by Baron Hiranuma
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A War Department routing slip transmitting an intelligence report on Japan to the State Department Far Eastern Division.
subfiles.from: Military Intelligence Division, War Department
subfiles.summary: Standard Military Intelligence routing sheet circulates a Japan intelligence report to military branches and the State Department's Far Eastern Division.
subfiles.title: Military Intelligence Division Routing Slip to Far Eastern Division
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: An ONI transmittal memorandum requesting that an attached report on Japan be forwarded to the State Department.
subfiles.from: Office of Naval Intelligence, Navy Department
subfiles.summary: ONI asks Major Crane to forward an attached Japan intelligence report to State's Far Eastern Division once the War Department finishes review.
subfiles.title: ONI Memorandum for Major Crane on Transmittal of Japan Report
subfiles.to: Major Crane, Military Intelligence Division, War Department

subfiles.about: An intelligence report analyzing upcoming Diet legislation, the controversy over the South Manchuria Railway presidency, rising fascist organizations, and White Russian activities.
subfiles.from: Naval Attaché, Tokyo / Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.summary: ONI Report 8 previews the May 1932 Diet session, tracing Inukai's Seiyukai government capitulating to the Army over South Manchuria Railway leadership, and rising Japanese fascist groups under Adachi and Nakano, plus a Kobe Semyonov-Araki-Tokonami meeting.
subfiles.title: ONI Report No. 8: Comments on the Political Situation
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A State Department analytical memorandum summarizing ONI Report No. 153 and evaluating three translated articles on military thought and Pacific strategy.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Salisbury summarizes ONI Report 153's three enclosures: Araki's 'back to Asia' pamphlet, a Japan-Hawaii Times piece on Hawaii's Japanese population (deemed unimportant), and Ishimaru's warning Japan would likely lose against an Anglo-American coalition.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Summary of ONI Report No. 153 on Translations of War Articles
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A comprehensive ONI report transmitting translations and summaries of War Minister Araki's nationalist pamphlet, an article on Hawaii defense, and a naval strategic study on a Pacific war.
subfiles.from: Naval Attaché, Tokyo / Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.summary: Report No. 153 provides an unabridged embassy translation of War Minister Sadao Araki's pamphlet promoting the Imperial Way, justifying military action in Manchuria and Mongolia as a moral mission to preserve peace, and discussing the status of Korean settlers in Manchuria and Siberia. The second enclosure summarizes an article by Shoichi A. Asami of the Nippon Jiji (Honolulu) discussing Representative Fred Britten's bill for military government in Hawaii and American fears of Japanese disloyalty. The third enclosure details Lieutenant Commander Tota Ishimaru's analysis of a future Pacific war, examining naval treaty ratios, cruiser and battleship deficiencies, the vital importance of Soviet neutrality, and the severe danger to Japan of an Anglo-American coalition.
subfiles.title: ONI Report No. 153: Translations of War Articles
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum highlighting army setbacks in Manchuria, anti-American propaganda, and Soviet pact overtures reported by the Tokyo Naval Attaché.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Salisbury summarizes an October 1932 Naval Attaché report on resurgent conservative influence, the Army's lost face over Manchurian bandits despite 75-80,000 troops, an Omori robbery used for anti-communist propaganda, and Araki rebuffing a Soviet nonaggression proposal.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Summary of ONI Tokyo Report of October 22, 1932
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: An ONI intelligence dispatch covering Japanese reactions to the Lytton Report, military difficulties in Manchuria, political maneuvers involving General Ugaki, and Soviet diplomacy.
subfiles.from: Naval Attaché, Tokyo / Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.summary: Attaché reports conservative resurgence under Takahashi against Araki, Minseito rumors of recruiting Ugaki, failed Manchurian operations against insurgents, a manufactured Omori robbery diversion blamed on communists, and debate over Chiang alignment, North China autonomy, or war with Russia.
subfiles.title: ONI Dispatch: Political Developments, Manchurian Situation, and the Omori Bank Robbery
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A State Department digest of the Tokyo Naval Attaché's bi-weekly summary covering cabinet politics, the death of Kaku Mori, Yasukuni Shrine disputes, and economic conditions.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Salisbury digests a December 1932 intelligence summary: Seiyukai maneuvering, fiscal tax/military tension, Mori's death, Geneva-Nagoya radio traffic, naval liaison transfer to Hsinking, Catholic-school Yasukuni disputes, American-policy reactions, rising prices, and 250 communist arrests in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Summary of Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of December 16, 1932
subfiles.to: Eugene H. Dooman / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A bi-weekly intelligence summary reviewing domestic political maneuvers, Shanhaikwan hostilities, Manchurian diplomacy, naval-military changes, and industrial mergers.
subfiles.from: Naval Attaché, Tokyo / Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.summary: The summary examines Seiyukai and Minseito party alignments toward the Cabinet and the political void left by the death of Kaku Mori. It reports on minor clashes at Shanhaikwan, commercial treaty negotiations with Manchukuo, and General Koiso's statements dismissing the need for a Soviet non-aggression pact. Naval and military entries record the sinking of the destroyer Sawarabi, army controversies with Catholic schools over Yasukuni Shrine homage, and Shinsaku Hirata's newspaper critique of unchecked military expenditures. Economic and social developments include falling postal savings, large-scale amalgamations in shipping (NYK, OSK, Kinkai Yusen Kaisha), steel, and paper, unemployment relief bills, and government-directed emigration to Manchukuo.
subfiles.title: ONI Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of December 16, 1932
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A brief State Department memorandum summarizing an ONI report on an air defense blackout drill held in Kobe.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Salisbury summarizes a purser's account of simulated Kobe air-raid drills, noting rigorous blackouts and public enthusiasm as evidence of underlying war sentiment in Japan.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Summary of ONI Report on Kobe Air Raid Practice
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: An ONI report detailing civilian blackout compliance, street demonstrations, and public enthusiasm during a simulated night air raid in Kobe.
subfiles.from: Office of Naval Intelligence (San Francisco Branch)
subfiles.summary: Kingsbury describes a simulated Kobe night air raid: door-to-door blackout enforcement, crowd pressure on a lit house, and cheering crowds watching searchlights, seen as popular war-readiness.
subfiles.title: ONI Report: Air Raid Practice at Kobe, Japan
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum summarizing the Tokyo Naval Attaché's report of January 27, 1933, regarding Diet tranquility, Manchurian campaign costs, Russian whalers, and army swords.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Salisbury digests a January 1933 summary: an unexpectedly calm Diet opening, Manchuria operations costing ¥573 million without local goodwill, detained Russian whaling vessels, new army-sponsored Defense Societies, and traditional swords replacing Western sabers.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Summary of Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of January 27, 1933
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A comprehensive intelligence summary detailing Diet political maneuvers, Soviet whaler detentions, mandate island defense rumors, naval programs, and May 15 court-martial trials.
subfiles.from: Naval Attaché, Tokyo / Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.summary: The Naval Attaché reviews political accommodations in the Diet, where Seiyukai leader Dr. Suzuki avoided confronting the Cabinet after failing to secure military backing. International topics include Soviet protests over Japanese communiqués, the detention of four Russian whaling ships at Futami in the Bonin Islands on espionage charges, and Japanese rebuttals at the League regarding alleged naval fortifications in Palau and Saipan. Naval entries detail Diet debates on the Imperial Command, construction of the destroyer Hatsuharu and river gunboats for Manchukuo, and air base work at Saeki. Economic and social sections report rising foreign trade deficits, bond sales by the Bank of Japan, nationwide petitions for leniency toward officers tried for the May 15 assassinations, labor strife at Osaka Iron Works, and 1930 imperial census statistics.
subfiles.title: ONI Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of January 27, 1933
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum highlighting fleet maneuvers, economic warnings, and colonial communist arrests from the Tokyo Naval Attaché's January 14, 1933 summary.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Salisbury highlights an August naval-maneuver notice near the Bonins, warnings of a coming economic reaction to Japan's export boom, mass Taiwan/Korea communist arrests, and a 25,000-emigrant Brazil subsidy plan.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Summary of Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of January 14, 1933
subfiles.to: Eugene H. Dooman and M. F. Perkins / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: An intelligence summary covering Cabinet instability, the Shanhaikwan clash, direct diplomacy versus the League of Nations, naval aviation, and colonial communist crackdowns.
subfiles.from: Naval Attaché, Tokyo / Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.summary: The report examines the Saito Cabinet's weakness, Seiyukai opposition to railway spending cuts, and debates over Navy Minister Admiral Okada's retirement age status. In foreign affairs, Japan pursued direct negotiations while threatening League withdrawal, as fighting erupted at Shanhaikwan and Japanese forces pushed toward Jehol and Pogranichnaya. It details allegations in the Japanese press of American aviation assistance to China, the formation of the Great Asia Association to promote an Asiatic Monroe Doctrine, and justifications for increased military spending. Further sections cover the municipal donation of Ueda airfield in Nagano, the end of search efforts for the sunken destroyer Sawarabi, pending exchange control legislation, suppression of communist conspiracies in Taiwan and Korea, and state-assisted emigration to Brazil.
subfiles.title: ONI Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of January 14, 1933
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum summarizing the Tokyo Naval Attaché's report of December 2, 1932, covering party politics, budget compromises, and social unrest.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Salisbury analyzes a December 1932 summary (first by Smith-Hutton): party disillusionment, reduced Army/Navy budgets (¥447M/¥372M), Lytton Report nationalism, rising recruitment, 35,000 schoolgirls' military training, steel/paper mergers, a hushed Tottori peasant uprising, and denial Araki threatened Baron Goh.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Summary of Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of December 2, 1932
subfiles.to: Eugene H. Dooman and Maxwell M. Hamilton / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: An intelligence summary covering party intrigues against the Saito Cabinet, Cabinet approval of the 1933-1934 defense budget, League diplomacy, and industrial amalgamations.
subfiles.from: Lieutenant Henri H. Smith-Hutton / Naval Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Written by Assistant Naval Attaché Lieutenant Henri H. Smith-Hutton, this summary assesses party dissatisfaction with the Saito Cabinet, the remote prospects of a Minseito cabinet under General Ugaki, and military dominance over politics. The approved 1933-1934 budget allocates 820,494,000 yen (35 percent of the budget) to the military, financed via public deficit bonds. The report details national excitement over Geneva League proceedings, Japanese rejection of President Hoover's disarmament proposals, and a surge in military and naval academy applicants. Economic and social sections report yen depreciation, the creation of a semi-governmental steel merger centered on Yawata Iron Works, paper company mergers, and significant strikes among seamen and university students.
subfiles.title: ONI Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of December 2, 1932
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum noting an attaché report on Japanese Diet interpellations concerning responsibility for determining military strength.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Salisbury summarizes a February 1933 report on Diet interpellations over constitutional responsibility for military strength, noting the Far Eastern Division had already received this information.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Summary of ONI Report on Military Strength Interpellations
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: An intelligence report analyzing Diet debates and the Legislative Bureau's ruling on the constitutional procedure for deciding military strength under the Emperor's Supreme Command.
subfiles.from: Naval Attaché, Tokyo / Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.summary: ONI Report 13: Diet interpellations questioned whether Saito/Araki upheld Hamaguchi's naval-limitation doctrine; the Legislative Bureau ruled military-strength decisions need coordinated military-civil counsel to the Throne, though the military demanded independent General Staff authority.
subfiles.title: ONI Report No. 13: Official Interpretation of the Procedure in Deciding the Military Strength
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence / Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum summarizing the Tokyo Naval Attaché's report of February 24, 1933, on public war fever over the League, naval rumors, and social legislation.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Salisbury summarizes a February 1933 report: intense public anxiety over League withdrawal, a Navy readiness alert, resentment of the U.S. Scouting Fleet, rumored Singapore-base/war-debt offers, Matsuoka possibly replacing Debuchi, Pacific Mandate exploitation, and legalized Japanese-Formosan marriages.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Summary of Bi-Weekly Intelligence Summary of February 24, 1933
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
